candidates.statement: The finished products for which notifications must be submitted under section 506C of the 105 FD&C Act (referred to in the guidance as covered finished products ) are prescription drugs and 106 biological products 18 (including blood or blood components for transfusion) that are (1) life 107 supporting, life sustaining, 19 or intended for use in the prevention or treatment of a debilitating 108 disease or condition, 20 including any such product used in emergency medical care or during 109 surgery or any such drug that is critical to the public health during a public health emergency 110 declared by the Secretary under section 319 of the Public Health Service Act; and (2) not 111 radiopharmaceutical drug products or any other products designated by FDA. 21 , 22 In addition, the 112 manufacturers listed above must submit notifications under section 506C of the FD&C Act for 113 API of covered finished products. 23
candidates.context: 17 See § 310.306, which applies § 314.81(b)(3)(iii) in its entirety to covered drug products marketed without an approved NDA or ANDA. candidates.statement: orders or meet expected demand for its product. 30 In other words, the assessment is to be based 167 solely on the reporting manufacturer’s capacity and supply. The manufacturer should not 168 consider other manufacturers’ or competitors’ capacities or assumed capacities, or what it 169 understands about market demand for the product. 31 To the extent it is possible to do so, 170 manufacturers must notify FDA of an interruption in manufacturing that is likely to lead to a 171 meaningful disruption in their own supply of the covered finished product in the United States 172 prior to the interruption’s occurrence. 32 In all cases, manufacturers should notify the Agency 173 before a meaningful disruption in their own supply of a covered finished product occurs. For 174 example, FDA should not first learn of a meaningful supply disruption resulting from an 175 interruption in manufacturing when a manufacturer is unable to fill an order. Note that after 176 providing the initial notification of an interruption in manufacturing of a covered finished 177 product under section 506C of the FD&C Act, FDA recommends that manufacturers provide 178 updates approximately every 2 weeks on the situation, including the expected timeline for 179 resuming normal operations, even if the status remains unchanged. These updates are important 180 to ensure that FDA remains informed and can act on the most current information. We 181 recommend that such updates be submitted until the situation has been resolved. 182
candidates.context: 29 See section 506C(a) of the FD&C Act; §§ 310.306(b), 314.81(b)(3)(iii)( a ), and 600.82(a). If a manufacturer is unsure of whether to notify FDA of an interruption in manufacturing 184 because the firm does not know whether it is likely to lead to a meaningful disruption in its 185 supply, 33 FDA urges the manufacturer to submit a notification anyway. This would allow FDA 186 to monitor the overall market and take timely steps, as necessary, to help prevent or mitigate any 187 resulting shortage. In addition, if a manufacturer is considering taking an action that may lead to 188 a meaningful disruption in the supply of a product (e.g., holding production to investigate a 189 quality issue or transfer of ownership), FDA requests that the manufacturer notify FDA 190 immediately through the process explained below in section III.E. 191

candidates.statement: In the case of interruptions in manufacturing of API, a covered finished product manufacturer is 193 required to notify FDA of interruptions in the manufacture of the API of such products that are 194 likely to lead to a meaningful disruption in the supply of API. When assessing whether a 195 meaningful disruption is likely to occur in this context, the manufacturer should consider 196 whether a change in production of the API is likely to lead to a reduction in the supply of API by 197 the API supplier that is more than negligible and would affect the API supplier ’s ability to fill 198 orders or meet expected demand for the API. 34 As noted in section III.A, to ensure the 199 manufacturer is able to satisfy the notification requirement with respect to API, manufacturers 200 should establish a process to ensure they receive sufficient, timely information about changes in 201 production of their supplier’s API. 202
candidates.context: As described above, the notification requirements under the FD&C Act and FDA’s regulations 204 are triggered by a permanent discontinuance or an interruption in manufacturing that is likely to 205 lead to a meaningful disruption in supply of certain finished drugs or biological products or API 206 for those products. However, FDA requests that manufacturers also notify the Agency when they 207 are unable to meet demand for covered finished products, even in the absence of an interruption 208 in manufacturing, for example, when there is a sudden, unexpected spike in demand. Though 209 manufacturers are not required to report this type of situation to FDA, reporting under these 210 circumstances provides an important signal to the Agency about a potential shortage and allows 211 FDA to take appropriate steps to address the potential shortage. 212

candidates.statement: Manufacturers should submit a separate notification for each permanent discontinuance or 357 interruption in manufacturing. A single initial notification may include a list of all affected 358 covered finished products 48 or API. Manufacturers should not provide notification about a newly 359 affected product (e.g., a new strength) in an update, even if the issue is related to a previously 360 reported interruption in manufacturing. Rather, a separate initial notification should be submitted 361 to ensure the newly affected product is tracked appropriately. In addition, as explained in section 362 II, notifications submitted to FDA to satisfy other reporting requirements (e.g., under section 363 506I of the FD&C Act) are not a substitute for the notifications required under section 506C. 364
